answer: Weighted history premium. Each action’s influence is scaled by prior paid activity, so a fresh identity enters at a low-weight river of near-zero impact and must spend real fees to climb. Every new account also pays a violet surcharge proportional to the total identities already funded from the same payment source, making mass creation linearly more expensive. A prism rule splits that penalty across shared wallets, so one funder’s tenth identity costs far more than its first. The attacker’s per-identity cost rises with each copy, while honest single identities pay the base rate.
